For each realization in a single-output reciprocal link with noiseless over-the-air return, this is equivalent to the negative returned gradient being a descent direction for all residuals and differentiable losses with nonzero error signals. Return noise is treated exactly. For isotropic fields, ball-shaped apertures, unshifted lattice points, and dilations approaching the critical covering radius, every minimizer is a deep hole except with exponentially small probability. A Gaussian vector on the deep holes determines the limiting failure probability, with explicit covariance and lattice-independent limiting normalization. Square, hexagonal, simple cubic, and body-centered cubic lattices have two, three, four, and twelve sign classes. At fixed target failure probabilities below the critical limiting value, this covariance determines the exact leading aperture constant. When the margin and target failure probability vanish jointly, that constant is common to lattice shapes within each dimension. A cubic correction yields vanishing relative tail error in a moderate-deviation regime. A non-asymptotic two-sided aperture law has explicit constants. With a Rayleigh-faded specular path and positive diffuse margin, a failure floor occurs at every positive path power exactly when the cosine of its phase change is negative somewhere in the cell. The floor vanishes for all directions exactly when the covering radius is at most a quarter wavelength.

item.title: The Capacity of Private Information Retrieval from Coded Storage Systems with Colluding, Robust and Byzantine Servers
item.description: arXiv:2610.37412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of private information retrieval from MDS-coded databases with $T$ colluding servers, $U$ robust servers, and $B$ Byzantine servers, referred to as U-B-MDS-TPIR. In the U-B-MDS-TPIR setting, $M$ files are stored across $N$ servers, and in this paper each file is independently encoded using an $(N,K)$ GRS code. We characterize the capacity among linear, full support-rank U-B-MDS-TPIR schemes as $C=\frac{N-U-2B}{N-U}(1+\frac{K+T-1}{N-U-2B}+\cdots+(\frac{K+T-1}{N-U-2B})^{M-1})^{-1}$ when $N-U-2B\ge KT$. When $K=1$ or $T=1$, the same expression gives the capacity without the linearity and full support-rank restrictions. We further extend the construction to the retrieval of $P$ out of $M$ files. For $P \ge \frac{M}{2}$, the resulting multi-file scheme achieves capacity when $K=1$ or $T=1$.

item.title: Privacy-Preserving Over-the-Air Federated Learning over Cell-Free Massive MIMO System with User-Centric Clustering
item.description: arXiv:2610.37424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates cross-layer design for differentially private federated learning over cell-free massive MIMO networks with over-the-air (OTA) aggregation. Distributed access points (APs) collaboratively serve user equipments (UEs) through user-centric clustering, where clipped local model updates are perturbed with Gaussian noise and simultaneously transmitted over a shared uplink for OTA averaging at a central processing unit. Exploiting channel hardening, we show that thermal noise inherent in wireless reception can act as a privacy-masking resource, reducing or even eliminating the need for artificial noise. Based on this observation, we formulate a joint optimization problem over AP-UE associations, UE transmit powers, and artificial noise variances to minimize aggregation variance subject to per-UE zero-concentrated differential privacy constraints derived from an ergodic privacy accounting framework. Analysis reveals a regime-dependent structure: stringent privacy requirements favor low transmit powers and sparse AP associations to exploit thermal noise for privacy, whereas relaxed requirements favor larger clusters to improve aggregation quality. The resulting mixed-integer nonconvex problem is solved via alternating optimization combining difference-of-convex power allocation and greedy coordinate-descent clustering. Numerical results show up to 89% lower aggregation variance than conventional baselines and enable 97% test accuracy on MNIST with consistent gains on CIFAR-10. Under strict privacy budgets, competing schemes remain near random-chance performance, while under relaxed budgets they continue to lag significantly behind the proposed design.

item.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a positive global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a positive local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. Our main tool is a reduction of $s$-principal compression to a rank-$k$ singular value perturbation. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

item.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.36727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.

item.title: Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.36964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How many fixed points does belief propagation have on a binary pairwise model? Over complex parameters, the admissible equations of a finite loopless multigraph form an algebraic family whose generic degree we determine: it is a graph state sum over edge sets without vertices of degree one, each vertex of positive degree contributing one less than its degree. We give two geometric realizations of this state sum. The first is the total Betti number of a universal edge-incidence ring constructed without parameters. Its full graded Betti table is the state sum, its Tor algebra is natural for noncontracting graph maps, the alternating numerator recovers the graph polynomial of Watanabe and Fukumizu, and an Artin reduction by a regular sequence realizes the one-variable specialization, corrected for tree components. The second lies in the actual family: at the strong-field boundary each state factor is a ramification index, and at sufficiently strong field the state charts exhaust the admissible complex fiber. For fixed nonzero real couplings, every Eulerian message-sign sector contains a real fixed point at every external field, and strong fields attain this lower bound: one admissible real fixed point per element of the binary cycle space and one positive fixed point. For graphs of maximum degree at most three, this minimum equals the number of minimal module generators of the edge-incidence ring. One state decomposition connects the complex degree, graded syzygies, and an attained minimum real count. The degree, selected ring and resolution statements, and the real counts are formalized in Lean 4.

item.title: Negative Results for Reciprocity-Based Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging: Stability, Alignment, and Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.37188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In reciprocity-based over-the-air split learning, channel aging rotates and attenuates the derivative signal returned to the transmitter. Seven case studies combine numerical forecasts, mechanism checks, and competing predictions. Near the correlation zero, an archived SGD comparison finds truncated inversion 0.000813 lower in cross-entropy than polar correction, with a paired 95% interval for the difference from -0.001853 to 0.000060, and a retained-mode quadratic proxy slightly favors truncation. Selecting the return port with the largest received power falls short of the predicted five-point alignment advantage over random selection at both tested spacings, gaining at most 0.97 points, while the local inverse relation between amplitude and phase gradient is supported. Seven specified interference-induced accuracy-collapse predictions are rejected, and independent zero-mean interference preserves the conditional mean under a fixed linear chain. Per-subcarrier correction and spherical-wavefront compensation do not deliver their predicted accuracy gains. Focusing leaves both methods near chance in a single-mode model and adds no observed gain in a model with a line-of-sight component plus scattering. A successful port assignment under nonsymmetric motion refutes an exact-symmetry requirement. The competing positioning-error prediction is supported. Gaussian rail jitter with a standard deviation of 0.383 wavelengths yields high terminal test accuracy, whereas a fixed bias of the same magnitude yields near-chance accuracy. These cases distinguish valid local physical relations from unsupported training forecasts through task support, noise injection, and update moments.

item.title: Code uniqueness of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in spatial chromatic model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The spatial chromatic model (SCM) is a novel entity-oriented spatial data model proposed in recent years. Spatial tessellations formed by SCM have been applied in preliminary analyses of spatial point pattern recognition,spatial topology, and Voronoi diagram generation. Unlike previous spatial tessellation models, a key feature of SCM is that each subspace (cell) possesses a chromatic code, which serves as the foundation for various theoretical analyses and applications of SCM. The uniqueness of cell cluster codes in SCM constitutes an important property of the model. Previous studies have demonstrated the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 2-cell and 3-cell connected disjoint clusters. Building on this analysis of connected cluster code characteristics, this paper proves the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters. The proof results and the new concepts introduced in this study help further refine the spatial chromatic model and provide a theoretical foundation for its subsequent applications.

item.title: A Constructive Method to Maximize Entropy under Marginal Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2601.09347v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of maximizing R{\'e}nyi entropy of order $2$ (equivalently, minimizing the index of coincidence) over the set of joint distributions with prescribed marginals. A closed-form optimizer is known under a feasibility condition on the marginals; we show that this condition is highly restrictive. We then provide an explicit construction of an optimal coupling for arbitrary marginals. Our approach characterizes the optimizer's structure and yields an iterative algorithm that terminates in finite time, returning an exact solution after at most $p-1$ updates, where $p$ is the number of rows.

item.title: Local Differential Privacy for Molecular Communication Networks
item.description: arXiv:2603.00690v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Molecular communication (MC) enables information exchange in nanoscale sensor networks operating in biological environments, yet privacy remains largely unaddressed. We integrate local differential privacy (LDP) into diffusion-based MC by privatizing each user's measurement at the transmitter and conveying the resulting randomized report over the MC channel. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic LDP implementation for diffusion-based MC, enabling privacy-preserving aggregate data analysis for in-body health monitoring and other population-scale sensing applications. We benchmark major LDP mechanisms under a realistic channel model. Simulation results show that Optimized Local Hashing (OLH) achieves the lowest average $\ell_1$ distribution-estimation error under the MC channel when channel resources are sufficient and the number of possible user values (alphabet size) $k$ is moderate to large, whereas k-ary Randomized Response (KRR) and, for privacy budget $\epsilon=1$, Binary Local Hashing (BLH), which have shorter reports, are more robust as the MC transmission quality deteriorates. We further propose RLIM-LDP, which combines run-length-limited ISI-mitigation (RLIM) coding with LDP coding. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that RLIM-LDP improves end-to-end reliability and reduces the final distribution-estimation error when time and molecule resources are limited.

item.title: Fast Fault-Tolerant Decoders for Hypergraph Product and Lifted-Product Codes
item.description: arXiv:2608.31040v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We design low-complexity, fault-tolerant decoders for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes with the goal of reducing decoding latency. We target two major bottlenecks of decoding under the \emph{circuit-level} noise model: (i) post-processing via order-statistics decoding (OSD), and (ii) the large number of auxiliary variable nodes commonly introduced to represent CNOT-induced correlations during syndrome extraction. Our key observation is that propagating CNOT faults (\emph{hook errors}) create \emph{stabilizer-induced} trapping sets (TSs) that are intrinsic to hypergraph-product (HGP) and lifted-product (LP) constructions. Therefore, instead of modeling each such fault with an explicit correlation node and relying on OSD to clean up the resulting failures, we design message-passing decoders that resolve the corresponding \emph{stabilizer-induced} TSs directly. We obtain these decoders by deriving QLDPC decoders from decoders for the parent classical LDPC codes and using them collectively to correct broad families of \emph{stabilizer-induced} TSs. For CNOT faults that manifest primarily as syndrome errors, we show that their effect is equivalent to a data error together with syndrome-bit measurement errors. Consequently, given repeated measurements and a decoding graph that already includes nodes representing syndrome-bit errors, no distinct variable node is needed for each CNOT fault. Using a \emph{phenomenological} Tanner graph with nodes representing only data errors and syndrome-bit errors, simulations on LP codes show a significant improvement in logical error rate relative to BP+OSD. Moreover, the improved error correction relies on low-complexity finite-state iterative decoders, targeted for fast and low-latency FPGA implementation.

item.title: Collision-Free Schedule Acquisition through Slotted ALOHA: Scaling Laws and Fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2609.09934v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Goal-oriented sensing, estimation, and control benefit from prompt, regular access to task-relevant updates. Although 1-persistent age-threshold slotted ALOHA (1-pTSA) can self-organize into a periodic collision-free schedule, its acquisition transient can dominate finite-horizon performance. We propose role-protected counter-threshold slotted ALOHA (RP--CTSA), which separates reservation memory from the age of information (AoI). A scheduled singleton retains its phase after colliding with active contenders, whereas a collision involving multiple scheduled nodes releases them immediately; AoI resets only after a decoded update. The protocol requires individual acknowledgments and a binary RELEASE/HOLD indication, but no centralized phase assignment or identification of colliders. Let $n$ denote the number of nodes and $\Gamma_n$ the counter threshold. Under inverse-population access scaling, the acquisition dynamics admit an exact pure-death representation. When $\Gamma_n=n$, the acquisition time is $O(n^2)$; when $\Gamma_n\sim(1+\theta)n$, with $\theta>0$, it is $O(n\log n)$. Simulations confirm both regimes and show substantial finite-horizon AoI gains over 1-pTSA while preserving every collision-free schedule.

item.title: On different notions related to APN mappings
item.description: arXiv:2609.22394v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An APN mapping $F:\mathbb{F}_{2^n}\to \mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ is a polynomial characterized by the non-vanishing property on 2-flats. In this work, we analyze notions that are closely related to this property. To understand which $k$-flats of $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ remain flats under $F$, we study the $k$-breaking. The function $x^{-1}$ has been studied in the past in this context---we extend this study to general mappings and characterize the 2-breaking of APN functions. Recently, two generalizations of the APN property have been introduced: $k$-strongly non-normality and $k$-th-order sum-freedom. Sum-freedom generalizes the non-vanishing property of APN functions to higher dimensional flats. We provide in-depth observations of the relations between the breaking property, strongly non-normality and sum-freedom. We introduce a fourth concept called $k$-strongly breaking, which implies the breaking property. We derive several structural results for both notions and give a characterization of a subclass of APN functions in terms of the 2-strongly breaking property. We propose a different perspective of the non-vanishing property via a natural character transformation, which is closely related to the sum-of-square indicator of the components of $F$. We derive a precise value for the total sum of the sum-of-square indicators of $F$. With this approach, we provide a simple answer to Open Problem 4 in IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 52(9): 4160-4170, 2006. Moreover, it allows us to explore balancedness properties of polynomials, one of which characterizes component-wise APNness, for odd $n$, and provides a natural extension to any dimension. We show that Dillon's APN permutation and the Gold functions satisfy a related property, termed $k$-balanced, which is presented under our framework.

item.title: Black-Box Attack for IRS-Aided Communications with BER-Only Feedback
item.description: arXiv:2609.23112v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has emerged as a promising wireless technology for enhancing legitimate communications. In this paper, we investigate an IRS-assisted multiuser MISO downlink network in which an attacker reconfigures the IRS to degrade legitimate data transmission. Specifically, we consider a black-box attack setting in which the attacker has access to neither channel information nor symbol-level observations and can observe only the BER reported by each user. The objective of the attacker is to identify an IRS configuration that maximizes the minimum BER among all users under a limited budget of non-repeated tests. To address this BER-only black-box attack problem, we propose PRIS, an online search method that learns effective phase transitions from previous trials and progressively narrows the search from large-block modifications to single-element refinement. Specifically, an annealed user-balancing reward and prioritized replay are incorporated to exploit noisy BER feedback. Numerical results demonstrate that PRIS achieves a higher minimum BER than existing benchmarks.

item.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

item.title: Exploiting Pinching Antenna Systems in NOMA Covert Communication Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.29433v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) provide flexible transmitter-side radiation reconfiguration for high-frequency wireless communications. This paper applies PASS to non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) covert communication networks, where activated pinching antennas (PAs) transmit superimposed signals to a pair of users stochastically distributed within a rectangle. Two passive wardens respectively monitor the downlink transmissions intended for two users. More specifically, we derive the closed-form detection error probability (DEP) expressions for two wardens under bounded noise uncertainty. Then we analytically determine the optimal detection thresholds and minimum DEPs in the worst-case covert detection scenarios. The covert transmission rates of two users are further characterized by taking into consideration ideal successive interference cancellation and non-ideal successive interference cancellation at near user and intra-NOMA interference at far user. Numerical results are presented to confirm that: 1) PASS-NOMA is capable of providing higher covert rates relative to conventional orthogonal multiple access OMA schemes; 2) As the number of activated PAs begun to increase, the near user has ability to obtain a larger covert rate gain than far user; and 3) The DEP of PASS-NOMA networks is larger than that of both PASS-OMA and traditional antenna based NOMA in specific output power regions.

item.title: Pinching Antenna and Relay Assisted Joint Indoor Outdoor NOMA Communications with SWIPT
item.description: arXiv:2610.33367v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a unified downlink architec- ture for serving indoor and outdoor users from a shared multi-antenna rooftop base station (BS). To overcome severe building-penetration loss, the BS transfers information and radio- frequency (RF) energy to an indoor access point (AP) using simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). The AP harvests this energy and performs amplify-and-forward (AF) relaying, enabling self-sustained indoor communication. A movable waveguide-mounted pinching antenna (PA) further improves indoor coverage by adapting its position to the prop- agation environment. For outdoor transmission, zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming suppresses inter-group interference, while power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) supports multiple users within each group. We maximize the outdoor weighted sum rate (WSR) while satisfying stringent indoor and outdoor quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. The resulting nonconvex problem jointly optimizes the BS power fraction, SWIPT power-splitting ratio, PA position, and NOMA power allocation. To obtain an efficient solution, we develop a two-stage method based on alternating optimization (AO) and sequential quadratic programming (SQP). Numerical results show that the proposed architecture improves outdoor spectral efficiency while maintaining reliable, energy-sustainable indoor coverage. Increasing the BS array size further raises the indoor QoS- satisfaction probability toward unity, even under demanding rate targets.

item.title: When Multiple-Unicast Feasibility Is Equivalent to Single-Sink Routability
item.description: arXiv:2610.33655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In communication networks, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, achieving transmission rates unattainable by routing alone in many multicast settings. In multiple unicast, where each source sends a message only to its prescribed destination, a central question is under what conditions fractional routing suffices to attain the transmission rates supported by network coding. We prove that, for any given collection of multiple-unicast demands in an undirected network, if the maximum flow between every pair of distinct destinations is at least the total demand rate, then the following are equivalent in feasibility: multiple-unicast coding, multiple-unicast fractional routing, and simultaneous fractional routing of all source rates to any fixed destination. Verifying this pairwise maximum-flow condition and, when it holds, deciding feasibility of the given multiple-unicast demands require at most as many maximum-flow computations as there are destinations. As a direct corollary, we prove the Langberg--M\'{e}dard conjecture: if a directed network supports coded multicast of independent source messages at a common rate to every destination, then removing arc directions without changing capacities permits simultaneous fractional routing at that rate for all prescribed source--destination pairs.

item.title: Logarithmic asymptotics for polynomial threshold functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34378v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We count Boolean functions represented as the sign of a real polynomial of bounded degree on the $n$-dimensional cube. We prove that the logarithm of their number is asymptotic to that of the classical hyperplane-arrangement upper bound, uniformly over all degrees, with relative error $O((\log n)^2/n)$. We also obtain sharper additive and relative error estimates in particular degree ranges, including an additive error $O(n^2)$ between the logarithms throughout a small linear degree range and improved bounds just below the central degree. The proof combines probabilistic estimates for Reed--Muller codes with a deletion argument for sets of evaluation vectors, an entropy count, and a sharp-threshold estimate for expected rank deficiency.

item.title: Acceleration data-based robust on-board monitoring of hunting proximity in railway vehicles under uncertainty: A feasibility study
item.description: arXiv:2610.36122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The feasibility of on-board, real-time proximity assessment to railway hunting initiation under uncertainty arising from vehicle/track and other operational conditions is assessed. In this context, a novel method that classifies hunting proximity into one of several prespecified speed proximity intervals is introduced, based on a grey nonlinear vehicle model with parameters estimated from on-board acceleration measurements and model-based estimation of the Maximum Lyapunov Exponent (MLE) as a hunting proximity measure. The method's performance and robustness are assessed via Monte Carlo simulations using a MATLAB-based multi-body vehicle model and four operating scenarios. The method is shown to achieve excellent performance achieving 97.08 % classification accuracy, which marks a significant improvement over a potential alternative. Its robustness to faulty suspensions and hollow-worn wheels is also demonstrated, although certain performance compromise is observed under worn-track conditions.

item.title: Multichannel Sampling and Reconstruction in Multidimensional Shift-Invariant Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.36142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a multichannel sampling and reconstruction framework for multidimensional principal shift-invariant spaces based on a finite-dimensional polyphase representation. Periodic nonuniform shifts and derivative measurements are modeled as analysis channels, leading to a frequency-domain linear system relating the measurements to the polyphase components of the underlying coefficient sequence. Stable recovery is characterized through uniform singular-value bounds on the associated polyphase matrix, and explicit synthesis kernels are obtained from its Moore Penrose left inverse. The formulation applies to both separable and genuinely non-separable generators and includes several classical one dimensional sampling formulas as special cases. For irregular derivative measurements, where the periodic polyphase structure is no longer directly available, we develop an iterative reconstruction method based on local bivariate Hermite interpolation followed by orthogonal projection onto the shift-invariant space. A sufficient contraction condition is derived to guarantee geometric convergence of the iteration. Numerical experiments demonstrate the reconstruction performance for separable and non-separable generators and illustrate robustness to additive measurement noise and sampling-location perturbations.

item.title: MtReNIRS: A Self-Supervised Foundation Model for Transferable Neurovascular Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.36159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) offers a promising approach for monitoring the hemodynamic correlates of neural activity in naturalistic settings. However, existing modeling methods for fNIRS are largely confined to small-scale, single-session data with low sampling rates, driven by high heterogeneity in acquisition devices and optode montages. In addition, the complex spatiotemporal structure of fNIRS signals further restricts model scalability and transferability across settings. As a result, it remains unclear whether a single fNIRS encoder can learn representations that are usable across subjects, tasks, devices, and montages. Here, we show that a montage-aware masked autoencoder, pretrained on 12 public fNIRS datasets spanning 268 subjects and 567 recording hours, learns generalizable neurovascular representations that transfer across three external datasets. Our fNIRS foundation model, MtReNIRS, jointly encodes the slow hemodynamic nature of fNIRS, chromophore identity and cortical location by mapping heterogeneous montages onto a shared anatomical reference. MtReNIRS achieves cross-subject performance on par or better than fully supervised baselines and excels in few-shot within-subject calibration, where it outperforms prior state-of-the-art fNIRS models, while remaining robust to sparse montages. Our results indicate that montage-aware self-supervision yields physiologically grounded, transferable fNIRS representations, providing a scalable foundation for label-efficient brain-computer interfaces.

item.title: Structured Wavenumber-Domain Channel Estimation for LoS XL-MIMO
item.description: arXiv:2610.36609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-field line-of-sight (LoS) channels in extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems exhibit distinctive structural properties in the wavenumber domain. In this paper, we develop a structured wavenumber-domain channel estimation framework that first obtains an initial channel estimate using classical estimators and then refines it through a windowing-based refinement step that suppresses out-of-band noise by exploiting the localized spatial-frequency power distribution. The resulting estimate is subsequently enhanced through a convex constrained formulation that exploits the sparsity and low-rank structure of the wavenumber-domain channel. The corresponding sparsity and rank constraint bounds are selected using a conservative worst-case characterization over the relative position of the transmitter and receiver. Numerical results show that the proposed framework improves estimation accuracy, particularly at low signal-to-noise ratio, by effectively leveraging the structural properties of the wavenumber-domain channel.

item.title: Soft Temporal Alignment Distillation for Camera-to-mmWave Radar Human Activity Recognition
item.description: arXiv:2610.36637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides privacy?preserving human activity recognition (HAR), but sparse point clouds limit its representation of body structure and motion. We propose a cross-modal knowledge distillation framework in which a teacher trained on camera-derived two-dimensional (2D) human keypoints supervises a radar-only student. The stu?dent combines PointNet-based point-set encoding, bidirectional temporal modeling, segment-level aggregation, and lightweight shared latent-channel scaling. The teacher retains contextualized states at every time step, whereas the student summarizes the radar sequence into a small number of segments, making fixed timestamp correspondence unsuitable for feature transfer. Soft Temporal Alignment Distillation lets each student segment adaptively retrieve and aggregate teacher temporal evidence into its distillation target. Alignment denotes student-conditioned representation-space matching rather than chronological or monotonic registration. On the Multi-Modal Non-Intrusive 4D Human Dataset (MM-Fi), the method improves radar-only ac?curacy from 87.04% to 89.17%, achieving the highest mean accuracy among the evaluated established and recent distillation baselines. It also obtains higher mean accuracy and macro?averaged F1 score (macro-F1) than the radar student under most evaluated point- and frame-dropout settings. Adaptation to our independently collected millimeter-wave Office Human Ac?tivity Recognition Dataset (mmO-HAR) improves accuracy from 80.33% to 87.75%, supporting the transferability of the distilled radar representation. The teacher and alignment branch are removed after training, enabling privacy-preserving radar-only inference without additional sensing or computational branches.

item.title: Spatial MIMO Channel Rendering: A 3D Gaussian Splatting Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.36880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The achievable gains of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems depend on channel state information (CSI), whose acquisition consumes pilot and feedback resources for every user in every coherence interval. Meanwhile, the propagation environment that shapes the channel persists. Exploiting such information will help to greatly reduce the overhead of CSI acquisition. This paper investigates the spatial MIMO channel rendering problem, which learns a latent beamspace channel scene from sparse observations and renders the long-term transmit and receive beam pair power map at unobserved user locations. Motivated by 3D Gaussian splatting in visual scene rendering, the proposed MIMO Gaussian splatting (MIMO-GS) represents the scene with pairs of receive and transmit 3D Gaussians, projects them from the user and base station onto the corresponding beam domains, and accumulates the beam associations through beam pair splatting. On a simulated urban scenario and measured indoor channels, MIMO-GS renders 5.5 times faster than ray tracing without a calibrated replica. Applied to multiuser beam management, the rendered maps allow users and transmit beams to be scheduled without sounding while accounting for the inter-user interference, and the net sum rate reaches 98% of the genie-aided benchmark, 19% above a position-based predictor.

item.title: Placing the Beamspace Window on a Hopping Carrier: Bin Drift, Exact Capture and the Cost of Rounding
item.description: arXiv:2610.37067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A frequency-agile radar with a large digital array moves the spatial frequency of its look direction across the beams of a spatial FFT every time it changes carrier, so a beamspace adaptive processor must decide where to put its window at each hop. Because the beamspace transform is orthonormal, the output of the processor depends only on the span of the window, and a hop changes nothing but where the window sits. Centring the window exactly on the fractional bin of the look direction keeps the look vector fully inside it at every carrier, for the price of one phase ramp before the FFT. On a 32 by 32 array over 4 to 8 GHz the look bin drifts by 1.6 to 6.9 bins for look directions from u=0.2 to 60 degrees. Rounding to the nearest bin costs up to 1.34, 0.74 and 0.50 dB of look-direction capture for 3 by 3, 5 by 5 and 7 by 7 windows. In a three-jammer scenario with 41 carriers, a window frozen at the lowest carrier loses 39 to 60 dB at the worst carrier for a look direction of u=0.55, the exact window beats nearest-bin placement by 0.31 to 0.65 dB there, and the advantage reverses for a nine-beam window near broadside, where nearest-bin was 0.61 dB better.

item.title: Orthogonal Zadoff-Chu Based Pilot Design For Fractional Channel Estimation in MIMO-OTFS
item.description: arXiv:2610.37079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequence-based pilot design for fractional channel estimation in orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation for point-to-point multi-input multi-output (MIMO) scenarios. Orthogonal pilot sequences are assigned to each transmit antenna using ZF sequences. At the receiver, a correlation-based scheme is used to construct the signal for estimation. The estimation relies on a two-dimensional extension of the Aboutanios and Mulgrew (A&M) frequency estimation method. Simulation results show that the proposed approach achieves low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) while maintaining stable performance as the number of transmit antennas increases.

item.title: Approximation of the Narrowband Velocity Ambiguity Function in Near-Field Sensing Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.37084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates the velocity ambiguity function in the radiative near-field of a uniform linear antenna array. First, the general ambiguity function is formulated and the velocity cross-section at a target position is considered. The velocity vector is decomposed into radial and tangential components, which are analyzed separately. Next, the closed-form approximations for the velocity ambiguity function are derived and shown to be accurate despite relying on far-field approximations. The results show that the near-field regime does not improve radial velocity estimation, but enables estimation of the tangential velocity. Finally, the velocity ambiguity functions and the achievable resolution are analyzed for different array configurations. For tangential velocity estimation, MIMO and a collection of SISO radars offer improved ambiguity function and resolution as compared to the SIMO/MISO configuration.

item.title: Closed-Form Subspace Loss and Snapshot-Limited Dimension Selection for Beamspace MVDR Radar
item.description: arXiv:2610.37089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A beamspace minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) processor adapts a window of B beams instead of all N elements of a large array, trading a subspace loss that falls with B against a covariance estimation loss that rises with B for a fixed number K of training snapshots. We give the subspace loss of a DFT beam window in point jamming in closed form: exactly for any jammer power, and in the high interference-to-noise ratio (INR) limit through the Dirichlet kernel of the array. Combined with the known scaled-Beta law of sample matrix inversion (SMI) with a fixed transform, it gives a window size B*(K) for unloaded SMI. On a simulated 32x32 array with carriers from 4 to 8 GHz, noise jammers and Billingsley land clutter, the exact form is within 0.04 dB of the clairvoyant subspace loss for 25- and 49-beam windows at jammer levels from 10 to 50 dB. For a 9-beam window whose three columns are taken by three jammers near the target's elevation, the clutter that the form leaves out costs up to 5 dB. With the nominal K, B*(K) picks the lowest-loss window in all 30 cases with more than one runnable window. The rule is an oracle: it needs the jammer parameters or the true covariance, and errors of 0.25 bin rms in the jammer directions add a mean loss of 0.04 dB. With diagonal loading the best window was larger still wherever the rule chose more than the smallest window.

item.title: Robust PPG-Exclusive Heart Rate Estimation During Maximal Exercise Using Population-Based Priors
item.description: arXiv:2610.37132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: PPG is the main technology for wearable heart rate (HR) monitoring. However, motion artifacts during intense physical activity reduce its reliability due to spectral overlap with the cardiac signal. This study investigates whether severely contaminated PPG signals can yield reliable HR estimates without auxiliary sensors by leveraging prior knowledge of HR dynamics. We acquired simultaneous PPG and ECG signals from 21 subjects during a maximal cycloergometer test. Using Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation, we built HR evolution priors from the ground-truth ECG and applied Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) to align normalized HR curves and estimate a barycenter average. DTW aligns normalized HR curves with minimal error across all subjects, validating robust population-based priors. For each test subject, we combined the PPG Power Spectral Density (PSD) with the prior distribution to generate a "posterior PSD". We identified and ranked candidate HR trajectories using heuristic search within the "posterior PSD" and selected the most likely path. Our approach reduced mean absolute error (MAE) in BPM relative to the ground-truth ECG by a median of 63.3% (IQR: 47.3%-74.6%) compared to a PPG+accelerometer benchmark. These results show that physiological priors and DTW-based alignment enable robust, PPG-exclusive HR monitoring during high-intensity exercise.

item.title: Assessing BIOMASS Radiometric Stability using Permanent Scatterers
item.description: arXiv:2610.37400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monitoring the relative radiometric stability of the European Space Agency's BIOMASS P-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) requires separating instrumental and processing effects from temporal changes in the scene backscatter. This study investigates the use of permanent scatterers (PSs) as opportunistic references for estimating residual radiometric gains without dedicated calibration targets. The PS-based calibration (PSCal) framework combines amplitude-based scatterer selection with iterative maximum-likelihood gain estimation. Simulations assess detection and estimation performance under the limited number of acquisitions available in BIOMASS stacks, highlighting the importance of stringent selection thresholds and the dependence of estimation accuracy on scatterer abundance and signal-to-noise ratio. The approach is applied to datasets over Nairobi, Kenya, and Cordoba, Argentina. Over Nairobi, PSCal identifies an approximately 1 dB radiometric anomaly subsequently traced to a defect in radio-frequency interference mitigation, while the remaining acquisitions exhibit estimated gain variations generally within 0.1 dB. Over Cordoba, twelve acquisitions spanning two mission phases separated by approximately eight months yield residual gain variations on the order of 0.1 dB despite pronounced changes in the scene backscatter and acquisition geometry. Results were observed to be consistent with measurements from the BIOMASS Calibration Transponder (BCT) installed in New Norcia (Australia). These results demonstrate the potential of carefully selected P-band PSs to complement dedicated calibration infrastructure for relative radiometric monitoring and the detection of processing anomalies.

item.title: 5G Sensing for Human Pose Estimation with PRS-based CSI: An Experimental Demonstration
item.description: arXiv:2610.37435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an experimental study of device- free 2D human pose estimation using Channel State Information (CSI) extracted from downlink Fifth Generation (5G) Positioning Reference Signal (PRS). The proposed system employs a Next Generation Node Base (gNB) transmitting PRS to a User Equipment (UE) equipped with two receive antennas to measure the radio channel. The CSI is estimated using a least-squares (LS) method, and processed through amplitude smoothing and phase calibration. The resulting amplitude and phase representations are used as inputs to a deep learning model for pose estimation. We compare amplitude-only input with joint amplitude-phase training at a bandwidth of 20 MHz. The joint training outperforms the amplitude-only solution and achieves Percentage of Correct Keypoints (PCK) equal to 32.2%, 72.9%, and 84.2% below 10%, 30%, and 50% of the distance between left shoulder and right hip, respectively. These results demonstrate that standardized downlink 5G PRS-based CSI contains useful information for human pose estimation, even with a simple radio configuration and a relatively small dataset.

item.title: Coordinated and Uncoordinated Channel Tracking for High-Rate IoT in Distributed Massive MIMO With Low-Resolution ADCs
item.description: arXiv:2610.37508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates dynamic channel tracking for high-rate Internet of things (IoT) in distributed massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) with low-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), where pilot and data activities are decoupled, pilots are reused, and mobile channels evolve across access slots. We hereby develop a quantization-aware joint coordinated Kalman filter (Q-JCKF) for known pilot activity and a quantization-aware distributed probabilistic data association filter (Q-DPDAF) for uncoordinated access. For uplink analysis, we derive a closed-form statistical use-and-then-forget (UatF) expression for Q-JCKF and mixture-aware, pilot-conditioned, and long-term statistical UatF formulations for Q-DPDAF, together with the large-N pilot-reuse ceiling and a cross-access point (AP) association term with an O(epsilon) posterior-concentration bound. The proposed framework recovers JC-KF/PDAF in the ideal-ADC co-located limit, and quantifies the conditional loss of Kalman measurement information caused by finite-resolution quantization. We further characterize computational, memory, and fronthaul scaling: Kronecker-structured Q-JCKF reduces covariance-processing complexity, while groupwise Q-DPDAF limits hypothesis enumeration from 2^K to 2^{K_r} and enables parallel AP-local processing. Simulations corroborate the analytical and complexity outcomes, quantify ADC-resolution and pilot-access effects, and demonstrate improved lower-tail spectral efficiency, robust mobility tracking, near-ideal 4-bit performance, reliable Q-DPDAF activity inference, and substantial runtime reductions over legacy implementations and processing frameworks.

item.title: A Theory of Transmit-Receive-Manifold of Single-Photon Quantum-Dot Antenna Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2610.37542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quantum-dot array that receives a single photon is a collectively coupled antenna, and its receive manifold is not always the plane-wave manifold. So, this work aims to develop a complete transmit-channel-receive manifold model for quantum dot (QD) arrays. For the sake of validation, it considers a reference target pattern which can be obtained using classical array excitation.

item.title: EEG-Based Decoding of Musical Mode and Melodic Direction Using Empirical Mode Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2610.37148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has proven to be a powerful tool for decoding neural activity in real-life scenarios, including the perception and processing of emotions elicited by music. Among the various musical features that modulate these responses, musical mode and melodic direction (or contour) play a central role. This work proposes a novel EEG feature extraction framework based on Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to decompose EEG signals recorded during active piano performance for the detection of these two musical features. Energy-based descriptors were computed from the first four Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) obtained through EMD and used to train a Wide Neural Network classifier. The model performance was benchmarked against several standard classifiers commonly employed in EEG classification tasks. Two experimental scenarios were explored: intra-subject and intersubject. In the former case, the proposed framework achieved average accuracies of 84%, whereas in the inter-subject case, accuracies reached 81% on average using the first IMF, with AUC-ROC values of 0.9 on average in both cases. A frequency-domain analysis revealed a strong correspondence between the IMFs and conventional EEG sub-bands, except for certain specific frequency components that were not fully represented. Predominant activations were observed over the frontal, temporal, and parietooccipital regions, areas consistently associated with music processing. Furthermore, the proposed method demonstrated robustness to handedness, successfully classifying EEG data across participants regardless of their dominant hand. These findings highlight the potential of EMD-based feature extraction for identifying music-related neural patterns and contribute to advancing research in Music Information Retrieval (MIR), affective neuroscience, and the broader understanding of the neural encoding of musical structure.

item.title: AuRaSim: A Ray-Tracing Based Automotive FMCW Radar Simulator for Dynamic Scenarios
item.description: arXiv:2610.37403v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern simulators can generate synthetic camera and LiDAR data with accurate annotations for downstream tasks. In contrast, automotive radar simulation remains less mature because it requires not only a 3D engine to model dynamic objects in the scenes but also electromagnetic material properties, antenna configurations, wave propagation mechanisms, and coherent signal synthesis. Existing frameworks are either proprietary or overly simplified, limiting the scalability of radar raw measurements. This paper presents AuRaSim, a ray-tracing-based automotive frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar simulation framework for dynamic scenarios. Rather than implementing all components from scratch, AuRaSim builds on Blender for efficient dynamic-scene construction and Sionna RT for graphics processing unit (GPU) accelerated electromagnetic ray tracing, while introducing radar-specific adaptations for path-resolved propagation with complex coefficients, motion-aware Doppler modeling, and subsequently coherent multi-channel analog-to-digital converter (ADC) cube synthesis based on waveform configurations. Quantitative comparison between simulated and measured range-Doppler maps in digital-twin scenarios achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.147 and a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 16.93 dB, demonstrating the accuracy and fidelity of the synthetic signal. AuRaSim therefore provides a complete and extensible platform for reproducible automotive radar simulation and research. Project homepage: https://wangzhaoze.github.io/aurasim.

item.title: Optimal transmit field distribution for partially obstructed continuous radiating surfaces in near-field communication systems
item.description: arXiv:2510.26262v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper deals with the optimal synthesis of aperture fields for (radiating) near-field communications in obstructed environments. A physically consistent model based on knife-edge diffraction is used to formulate the problem as a maximization in Hilbert space. The optimal solution is obtained as a matched filter that ``matches" the shape of a diffraction-induced kernel, thus linking wave propagation with signal processing methods. The framework supports hardware implementation using continuous apertures such as metasurfaces or lens antennas. This approach bridges physically grounded modeling, signal processing, and hardware design for efficient energy focusing in near-field obstructed channels.

item.title: Unsupervised Learning for Scalable Downlink Power Control in Cell-Free Massive MIMO
item.description: arXiv:2605.26301v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output systems, downlink power control is essential to ensure uniformly high service quality across users. Existing solutions range from computationally demanding centralized optimization to scalable distributed schemes with limited fairness. This letter proposes an unsupervised, physics-informed framework that directly optimizes max-min fairness without optimal labels or user position information. The method scales with the number of UEs, requires no retraining when the number of UEs changes, and admits a fully scalable extension. Numerical results show that it nearly doubles the worst-user spectral efficiency over existing scalable schemes.

item.title: Time-Window Noise2Noise: Self-Supervised Blind Denoising of Mechanical Vibration and Impact Signals
item.description: arXiv:2608.24443v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vibration and impact measurements in mechanical systems are invariably corrupted by noise, which degrades every quantity derived from them, such as modal parameters and contact forces. Classical filters rely on assumptions about the noise or the signal, and linear filters cannot remove the noise that shares the frequency band of the structural response. This work presents Time-Window Noise2Noise (TWN2N), a self-supervised method for blind denoising of signals produced by deterministic mechanical systems. The method requires neither a clean reference signal nor paired noisy observations, nor a measured noise variance or distribution: by reconstructing each time instant from its temporal neighborhood while masking the instant itself, a compact autoencoder is encouraged to exploit the coherent temporal and multichannel structure of the measurement rather than the noise. The formulation requires no model of the system and is assessed on two benchmarks with exactly known ground truth: the impulse response of a linear 3-degree-of-freedom system and a nonlinear Hunt-Crossley impact. Over repeated realizations, TWN2N exceeds a zero-phase low-pass filter with oracle cutoff at low and moderate input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and gives the largest gain inside the structural band, which a linear filter largely preserves, among the Savitzky-Golay and wavelet references; the advantage vanishes at high input SNR and under brown noise. The benefit propagates to identification: the damping ratio of the weakest mode, overestimated several-fold on the raw signals, is recovered close to its reference value after denoising.

item.title: Sequential RF Fingerprinting for AIS: Rejecting Unknown Vessels and Insider MMSI Spoofs Days After Enrollment
item.description: arXiv:2610.19115v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Any AIS transmitter can claim any vessel's identity (MMSI), because nothing in the protocol authenticates it; only the transmitter's analog hardware reveals who is really sending. We treat AIS traffic as streams of bursts keyed by claimed MMSI and accumulate physical-layer evidence with a sequential test. Each burst is scored by its k-nearest-neighbor distance to enrolled fingerprints in the feature space of a classifier whose weights are fixed after training, calibrated into a tail probability, and accumulated by a geometric-entropy-minimization cumulative-sum (GEM-CUSUM) statistic. The same test rejects unknown transmitters when scored against all enrolled vessels, and exposes insider spoofs when scored against the claimed vessel. A threshold refreshed from genuine traffic alone keeps it at a stated false-alarm rate as fingerprints drift. On AIS in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) recordings captured over 13 days at the Istanbul Strait (Bosphorus), the detector rejects unseen vessels at least 10 days after enrollment. Evaluated over 50-burst trials with every vessel weighted equally, it reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.956 (95% confidence interval 0.913-0.989), where the best score computed from one burst at a time reaches 0.899. A threshold refreshed from the first quarter of the enrolled vessels' traffic holds 5.3% false alarms (3.0-9.2% across five independently trained encoders) at 88.8% detection. Scored against the claimed MMSI, enrolled transmitters spoofing another vessel are rejected at 0.991, a threat that open-set tests cannot see (AUROC 0.500, chance level). The lightweight Transformer GLFormer, reimplemented from its paper (no code is public) and retrained on the same data, reaches 0.652 in the same detector with its published in-phase input and 0.849 when given the same I/Q input as our encoder.

item.title: On the Performance of RIS-Empowered Transmitters with Receive Combining Techniques
item.description: arXiv:2610.26344v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-empowered transmitters offer a promising basis for hardware-efficient multi-antenna architectures in next-generation wireless networks. In particular, combining these transmitters with low-complexity reception techniques such as receive antenna selection (RAS) can further simplify the receiver architecture. In this paper, we investigate the impact of practical phase-shift constraint on RIS-empowered multi-antenna systems employing maximal ratio combining (MRC) and RAS. Since each RIS element can apply only a single phase-shift at a given time, the system performance degrades substantially when multiple receive antennas are active simultaneously. To quantify this effect, closed-form outage probability expressions are derived and asymptotic analyses are carried out over Rician fading channels. We show that the practical phase-shift constraint of RIS-based transmitters can degrade the diversity order of MRC and in addition, RAS outperforms MRC in the examined system models, contrary to the conventional performance ordering of these techniques.

item.title: Bodyseismography (BSG): Theoretical Foundation and Numerical Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.35844v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bodyseismography (BSG) records cardiovascular vibrations transmitted through the body and a supporting bed, enabling contactless assessment of cardiac mechanics. Relating these vibrations to hemodynamic features requires separating cardiac excitation from the effects of body and bed transmission. We develop a source-transmission-measurement framework that couples myocardial contraction and vascular recoil to directional BSG observations. The theory connects stroke volume, cardiac output, and blood pressure to observation and target Jacobians, establishes a local first-order target-observability criterion, and characterizes how additional sensing axes reduce ambiguities under specified source and transmission uncertainties. Numerical modeling combines four-chamber cardiac mechanics, cardiac-to-body excitation, and calibrated body-bed operators. Across 27 participants, a multilayer finite-element model with calibrated frequency correction achieves median Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.865 for the vertical channel and 0.682 for the planar-sum channel in matched-window waveform reconstruction. Controlled stroke-volume perturbations show that transmission reshapes feature sensitivity, including a reversal of the vertical feature association in 8 of 27 participant-specific transfer models. These analytical and numerical studies explain how cardiovascular sources and mechanical propagation jointly shape triaxial BSG and provide a physical basis for relating directional vibration features to hemodynamic changes.

item.title: Incremental-Smoothing-Based ARAIM Protection Levels for Tightly Coupled GNSS/IMU Integration in Urban Canyons
item.description: arXiv:2610.32259v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Protection levels (PLs) bound position errors under specified fault hypotheses and risk budgets, but advanced receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (ARAIM) is formulated for snapshot GNSS estimation rather than the correlated posterior of tightly coupled GNSS/IMU factor graph optimization (FGO). This paper formulates ARAIM solution separation and PL computation on the FGO posterior. Because current-epoch pseudorange factors enter only the current-state block of the fixed-lag information matrix, the fault-excluded position covariance, solution separation, and nominal-bias propagation follow exactly from the linearized current-state marginal, which re-tains correlations with velocity, IMU-bias, and clock states and with historical information. Woodbury updates with selected-output evaluation compute these quantities for fault-free, single-satellite, constellation-wide, and second-order hypotheses with-out repeated full-state inversion or graph reoptimization. Surrounding monitoring layers screen measurements, handle post-fit outliers, and determine PL validity and availability. In two road experiments, both nominal sequences achieve 100% horizontal and vertical empirical bounding over PL-valid epochs, with a maximum error-to-PL ratio of 0.96. Normalized errors show that the posterior covariance alone does not capture slowly varying ranging biases: a covariance-only bound computed from the same posteriors retains no resolvable margin, and strong temporal correlation limits the empirical evidence to consistency checks rather than validation of the integrity budget. On identical Experiment A posteriors, the proposed method reduces fault-hypothesis evaluation and PL solving time by 65.2% relative to direct full-state inversion with matching integrity decisions, and controlled fault injections demonstrate fail-safe PL invalidation while navigation continues.

item.title: Improving Learned AC-OPF Feasibility under Distribution Shift with PF-in-the-Loop Correction
item.description: arXiv:2610.36236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning-based AC-OPF enables fast dispatch, yet its feasibility can degrade under distribution shift. We analyze three state-of-the-art methods and identify a shared deployment-time limitation: none use feedback from the power-flow (PF)-realized state to ensure feasibility of the predicted control. Using a simple PF-in-the-loop feasibility restoration filter, we empirically show that such feedback substantially improves hard feasibility across four out-of-distribution scenarios with modest runtime overhead.

item.title: Distribution Grid Reconfiguration and Restoration via Linearizable Multi-phase Power Flow Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.36252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate and tractable power-flow (PF) modeling is essential for distribution grid topology optimization, where the presence of discrete branch-status decisions therein significantly increase the computational complexity. To tackle this challenge, we develop a topology-adaptive, low-complexity neural piecewise-linear (N-PWL) PF model. We propose a sequential layer design that can directly incorporate branch status variables into the PF mapping from branch flows to nodal injections. As a result, our N-PWL model not only preserves the PF branch-node consistency but also facilitates the representation of any unseen topologies without retraining. A low-complexity model design is further pursued to attain a linear NN parameter scaling by using a fixed-size area partition of the feeder. The resulting scalable N-PWL model enables mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations of feeder topology optimization tasks, including distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) and restoration ordering problems (ROP). Numerical studies on the unbalanced, multi-phase IEEE 123-bus feeder demonstrate our N-PWL model outperforms existing end-to-end baselines in PF prediction and, more importantly, can fill the gap by achieving accurate representation of any unseen topologies. For solving DNR/ROP, our model can significantly improve the AC feasibility over linearized PF models, with a notable reduction of computation time compared with AC-PF based nonlinear formulations, particularly under a large number of topology decisions.

item.title: Multi-time-scale Control of Power Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.36357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The power grid has been dominated by large synchronous generators and clearly separated control layers. Today, power-electronics energy conversion interfaces are rapidly being deployed calling for another look at system-level control hierarchies. This article examines how multi-time-scale modeling, feedback control, and feedback optimization can help reinterpret the traditional organically grown hierarchy of primary control, automatic generation control, and economic dispatch, and enable new approaches for control of contemporary power systems. Beginning with an overview of power system models and conventional operational practices, the article develops connections to modern control architectures that can coordinate heterogeneous resources, account for operational constraints, and exploit faster actuation without overlooking first-principles physics.

item.title: Data-Driven Hamiltonian for Neural Optimal Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.36378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a prominent data-driven approach to optimal control, but often requires substantial amounts of data and provides limited guarantees when encountering out-of-distribution state-action pairs. In this paper, we propose an alternative approach grounded in the well-established Hamilton-Jacobi framework in optimal control theory. Rather than requiring an explicit analytical model of the system dynamics to evaluate the Hamiltonian, we replace this with a data-driven Hamiltonian (DDH), which we generalize to a broad class of optimal control problems. In contrast to standard RL approaches, the DDH provides a principled mechanism, requiring only minimal prior system information such as a Lipschitz constant, for quantifying and accounting for uncertainty in regions not covered by the data, enabling the derivation of controllers with performance guarantees. Additional prior system knowledge, when available, can be readily incorporated to improve performance. For high-dimensional systems, we further introduce a physics-informed neural approximation of the value function, trained using a novel procedure that generates worst-case fictitious rollouts evaluated through the DDH. On an LQR problem, the DDH reaches near-optimal cost on every dataset we test, including random data on which offline RL methods remain far from optimal, and needs far fewer samples than online RL. On a nonlinear lunar lander benchmark, the DDH achieves an optimality gap to a trajectory-optimization reference more than $3\times$ smaller than CQL and FQL, and matches the performance of SAC with approximately $37\times$ fewer samples. These results establish the DDH as a promising framework for data-driven optimal control, particularly in settings where available data are limited in quantity or quality.

item.title: Electric Vehicle Scheduling and Carbon-Aware Energy Dispatch for Charging Stations
item.description: arXiv:2610.36426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations integrating photovoltaic (PV) generation, battery storage, and bidirectional grid exchange must coordinate access to limited chargers with energy supply while considering both energy cost and carbon emissions. This paper proposes a solver-free greedy heuristic (SFGH) for dynamic vehicle scheduling (VS) and a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) controller for carbon-aware energy dispatch (ED). SFGH assigns EVs according to reductions in service delays, and TD3 controls battery operation to balance energy costs and carbon emissions while meeting the resulting charging demand. The model allows both PV and battery exports, accounting for export revenue and carbon credits. Simulations on year-long case studies show that SFGH--TD3 achieves the lowest accumulated service delay, energy cost, and carbon emissions among the evaluated heuristic and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) configurations.

item.title: Phase-Coordinated Model Predictive Control for AI Training Power Smoothing
item.description: arXiv:2610.36441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodic power fluctuations from artificial intelligence (AI) training workloads can excite oscillations in power systems. This paper proposes a model predictive control (MPC) framework that exploits short start-time delays to mitigate power fluctuations at the computing source. By coordinating the relative phases of independent training jobs, the proposed method reduces the superposition of oscillatory power components without interrupting running jobs or requiring additional power-smoothing hardware. To obtain a tractable optimization formulation, cosine and sine projections are employed to quantify the dominant oscillatory power components, and their magnitudes are used to construct a convex quadratic power-smoothing objective. The receding-horizon framework updates launch decisions as new workload information becomes available while maintaining scheduling feasibility under limited computation time. Numerical results demonstrate reductions of 74.39\% in mean-square power fluctuations within the 0.2--2-Hz band and 46.6\% in power standard deviation, with an average launch delay of 2.188~s. All launch deadlines are satisfied, and the maximum end-to-end computation time is 0.390~s, below the 0.50-s MPC update period.

item.title: A Topology-Aware Neural Network for Fault Location With Missing Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.36474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a topology-aware neural network-based fault locator (TANFL) for radial distribution feeders, which uses voltage and current phasors obtained after the decay of fault induced transients, as well as feeder connection relationships and line parameters, as inputs. The shared bus encoder, bus readout module, and gated line readout module work together to identify the faulty bus or line and estimate the continuous fault location on the selected line. During training, explicit missing data indicators and random bus data block masking are introduced, enabling a single trained model to handle both complete measurement sets and scenarios where any permitted bus measurement device fails. On the IEEE 15 bus feeder, this paper compares TANFL with a conventional multilayer perceptron (MLP) and the formula-based localization method under identical data, measurement availability scenarios, and evaluation metrics. On the test partition, TANFL outperforms the conventional MLP; with complete measurements, its line fault location performance is slightly lower than that of the formula-based method, but in the average results for scenarios with one missing bus measurement block, its accuracy is the highest among the three methods at a 5% tolerance.

item.title: Thermal-Mass Coupled Modeling and Optimal Scheduling of Aluminum Smelting Loads for Safe Demand Response Participation
item.description: arXiv:2610.36555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aluminum smelting loads (ASLs) offer substantial flexibility potential, yet their actual participation in demand response remains conservative owing to the risk of operational failures. Power adjustments disturb the electrolyte temperature and superheat, which may lead to electrolyte freeze-out or yield loss. Existing ASL demand response methods often rely on oversimplified dynamic models of the electrolytic cell's thermal behavior, such as linear models and the Equivalent Thermal Parameter (ETP) model, which may either violate temperature constraints or underestimate the available flexibility. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a Thermal-Mass Coupled (TMC) dynamic model. The model captures the essential physical mechanisms of electrolytic cells, including alumina feed dynamics, ledge phase-change dynamics, and state-dependent current efficiency. The resulting nonlinear relations are reformulated into a tractable mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model using Taylor approximations and McCormick-envelope reformulations. In the illustrative PBDR and IBDR case studies, the nonlinear reference-model assessment shows that the TMC model achieves net economic improvements 122.4% and 325.1% higher, respectively, than the ETP model. The proposed framework can therefore support deeper demand response participation by aluminum smelters while explicitly assessing adherence to operational safety constraints.

item.title: Retrofitting centralized air compressor stations with end-use-aware predictive set-pressure control using a physics-constrained pressure-drop model
item.description: arXiv:2610.36678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compressed air systems usually run at a constant set pressure well above the end-use requirement; the excess margin is wasted energy. A lightweight hierarchical nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) scheme, retrofitted to the sequencing controller of a centralized compressor station typical of small and medium-sized plants, lowers the set pressure as far as the end-use requirement allows. It uses only two pressure gauges (receiver and one critical end-use point) and compressor data, without flow meters or piping surveys. The end-use pressure is predicted by a low-order pressure-drop model identified by least squares under stability, damping and steady-state equilibrium constraints, which serve use rather than accuracy: they let the measured pressure drop be held over the horizon with unit gain. Validated in three stages (plant data, a pipe-network simulator checked against measurements, and the actual controller, at most 1.41 s per update), the NMPC meets the required pressure under real demand and reduces the estimated annual energy consumption by 2.8 % relative to the current constant operation (9.3 % relative to 0.70 MPa). A PID cascade with the same gauge saves about as much only when tuned by a standard rule at its recommended setting from a constant-load step test, difficult in an operating plant; the NMPC needs no such test and keeps its performance with its initial model and default weights after plant expansion and network split. The margin becomes a design parameter instead of a fixed excess, and the controller's signals show where the supply system lacks headroom.

item.title: Whittle Index Policy for Three State Collapsing Bandits
item.description: arXiv:2610.36733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partially observable restless multi-armed bandit models have been studied for dynamic resource allocation problems under uncertainty. This paper analyzes three-state restless multi-armed bandits with partial observability. These are called collapsing bandit problems if the state of an arm (bandit) is perfectly observable when it is scheduled for allocation. The state is not observable when the arm is not scheduled. The planner has a budget constraint on the scheduling decisions in each time slot. The planner's goal is to maximize expected cumulative long term discounted reward. We study the Whittle index policy. To analyze index policy, first the $N$-armed collapsing bandit problem is decoupled into $N$ single arm problems, and convexity and monotonicity of the optimal value function in belief vector are derived using monotone likelihood ratio (MLR) ordering on state transition dynamics and monotone reward structure assumption. We next show that the optimal policy is of threshold type in belief under sufficiency conditions on the model. These sufficiency conditions depend on Lipschitz bound on the value function in the belief. We further prove the indexability for an arm using Lipschitz bound on subsidy sensitivity with minimal restrictive assumption on the transition probability model and discount factor $\beta.$ Our results generalize to three state and strengthen existing results on threshold policy and indexability with weaker model assumptions. We provide index computation algorithm and we present comparison of the Whittle-index, myopic policy and round-robin policies in the simulation study.

item.title: Co-Optimization of Network Topology and Variable Impedance Devices under Dynamic Line Ratings Using Iterative McCormick Relaxation
item.description: arXiv:2610.36871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs), such as Network Topology Optimization (NTO), Dynamic Line Rating (DLR), and Variable Impedance Devices (VIDs) are increasingly deployed in power transmission grids to address congestion and improve grid utilization. However, their growing adoption necessitates coordinated operation to fully exploit their benefits. This paper presents a unified co-optimization framework that integrates NTO, DLR, and VID to alleviate congestion and minimize operational costs. NTO is modeled using a node-breaker formulation to provide enhanced switching granularity, while DLR incorporates weather-dependent parameters, including wind speed and ambient temperature, to dynamically adjust transmission limits. The resulting formulation is a mixed-integer nonlinear program due to power flow constraints with bilinear VID terms, and discrete topology decisions. To improve tractability, we propose using a McCormick relaxation approach to linearize bilinear terms. Furthermore, we propose an iterative refinement of the McCormick relaxation scheme to enhance solution accuracy. The proposed framework is validated through detailed analyses on the IEEE 118-bus system, along with additional case studies on other benchmark systems to assess scalability.
